messages.subject: discrete latent variable examples
messages.body_plain:
Hi TMB users,

If anyone is looking for some exercises for a student or just a fun challenge, it would be useful to the community if someone worked out TMB code for models from the book "Bayesian Population Analysis using WinBUGS --- A Hierarchical Perspective" (2012) by Marc Kéry and Michael Schaub.

They have been worked out in Stan and documented here.
https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/tree/master/BPA
Similar to TMB, Stan can’t automatically integrate over discrete latent variables, so these examples show how to manually integrate over the discrete latent variables.

Cheers,
Mollie

messages.subject: Re: accuracy of the Laplace approximation
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am not aware of any generic feature in TMB (or in general) that will improve the Laplace approximation.
My advice would be to simulate from the assumed model and see if the resulting parameter estimates are biased (that is what
matters at the end of the day). Maybe this is what you already are doing ("parameter bias low").

Hans

> Hi all,
>
> I have a couple general questions about the accuracy of the Laplace approximation. I primarily work with GLMM spatial models where random effects follow a GMRF and data follow a variety of distributions such as delta-Gamma, Poisson, and Tweedie.
>
> I run the checkConsistency function on my models and get high marginal p-values. This test, however, only considers the expectations of the joint and marginal. Are there any new developments in TMB that check the 2nd order accuracy or improve the approximation in the tails? If the marginal p-value from the test is high and parameter bias low, how concerned do I need to be about higher order inaccuracies?
>
> I appreciate any feedback!
> Andrea
>

messages.subject: Re: accuracy of the Laplace approximation
messages.body_plain:
The checkConsistency function is a shortcut to performing a full simulation-reestimation experiment. You get essentially the same output i.e an estimate of bias assuming a given true parameter configuration. However, checkConsistency is faster and more numerically robust. One can think of checkConsistency as doing a single newton step from the true parameter towards the MLE, with the hessian replaced by the expected information matrix (guarantied to be positive definite). This usually provides a highly accurate estimate of the bias. So, to the question

"If the marginal p-value from the test is high and parameter bias low, how concerned do I need to be about higher order inaccuracies?"

I would claim that you don't need to be worried, but if in doubt you can always do a full sim-reestimation experiment as Hans suggests. Please report back if you get very different results than checkConsistency provides :)

Note that TMB already has an importance sampler option (samples drawn from the Gaussian posterior approximation).

library(TMB)
runExample("simple")
obj$env$MCcontrol$doMC <- TRUE
obj$env$MCcontrol$n <- 1000
obj$fn()

However, from experience it is not really useful for high dimensional models.

messages.body_plain:
Hi, I have encountered difficulty installing R (from source) and TMB on Linux Mint 19.3 (latest release). Specifically, I
downloaded the R source tarfile from the R CRAN and untared in a subdirectory of home
used the Software Sources utility to add the following source repos to the sources.list.d directory (Mint's way of doing this)

deb https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu bionic-cran35/

ppa:marutter/c2d4u
executed
sudo apt build-dep r-base (to install r-base dependencies)
./configure -enable-R-shlib
make
make check (all good)
sudo make install
The R install looked OK. Then I ran the TMB simple regression example (attached) in R Studio.

I got a huge number of warning messages, a sample of which is below, and then the final message indicating that the compile worked! The messages relate to accessing the installed TMB and RcppEigen subdirectories. Running the model indicated that it worked and produced the expected output. hmm....

Not clear at all what is going on. I thought that it might be something with the $PATH but the warning messages indicate that these directories are being accessed. Has anyone enountered this problem and can suggest a fix?

Bob

messages.subject: Re: TMB install in LInux Mint 19.3
messages.body_plain:
These warnings show up when installing any R package that depend on RcppEigen. It's a mystery to me why no one care to fix this. Anyway, it's a known problem with a known 'solution':

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/277

In short you have to tell the compiler that the warnings (hopefully) are harmless by adding to your ~/.R/Makevars something like:

EIGEN_SHUT_UP=-Wno-aggressive-loop-optimizations -Wno-deprecated-declarations -Wno-ignored-attributes -Wno-enum-compare -Wno-int-in-bool-context
CXXFLAGS+=$(EIGEN_SHUT_UP)

messages.body_plain:
Is it possible to pass a list of arrays (3d) in a similar way? There doesn't seem to be an `asArray<Type>` function. But, maybe there's a way with asVector and asMatrix?

On Friday, March 22, 2019 at 9:26:40 AM UTC-7, Kasper Kristensen wrote:
>
> Inspired by
> https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/96
> and
> https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/abbd69a1a684b4b8e442a4c73fbc41f3ba921540/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L372
> you could modify to something like (not tested):
>
>
> #include<TMB.hpp>
>
> /* List of integer matrices */
> template<class Type>
> struct LOIM_t : vector<matrix<int> > {
>   LOIM_t(SEXP x){  /* x = List passed from R */
>     (*this).resize(LENGTH(x));
>     for(int i=0; i<LENGTH(x); i++){
>       SEXP sm = VECTOR_ELT(x, i);
>       if(!Rf_isMatrix(sm)) Rf_error("Not a matrix");
>       (*this)(i) = asMatrix<int>(sm);
>     }
>   }
> };
>
> template<class Type>
> Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
> {
>   // x = list of sparse matrices
>   DATA_STRUCT(x, LOIM_t);
>   // Get the first...
>   matrix<int> y = x(0);
>   REPORT(y);
>   return 0;
> }
>
>

> >
> > The other way I thought to do it was to send a 3D array and slice it up in C++ but there doesn't seem to be an easy way to do that either.
> >
> > Andy

messages.subject: Re: Compile Output
messages.body_plain:
Answered my own question. For info, standard bash command &> as per

   compile("modelfile.cpp", "&> output_file")

output_file is text file with complete error listing in working directory (in this case)

Bob
